text:
ana: Heads-up — for the new compat shim rollout, we should avoid exploding metrics. Proposal: sample telemetry at 1% by default, with per-tenant opt-in to 100% for debugging. Thoughts?
devin: Agree. Also want tags to indicate shim type + migration-stage. e.g., `shim=header-normalizer,stage=canary`.
mike: One catch — sampling at proxy level can distort latency histograms. If we sample only events, we lose tail latency signals. Maybe emit lightweight counters for critical SLO breaches and sampled full spans.
sarah: Privacy check: don't include any tenant PII in tags. Also: sampling can't be reversed to reconstitute user activity.
devin: Implementation idea: add header `X-Compat-Telemetry: sample=0.01;mode=optin` and let shim read it. Pseudocode:
```
if header.sample < 0.1: emit_counter("shim.invoked")
else: emit_span("shim.request", attrs...)
```
ana: That header change is fine. For hosted default we set sample=0.01. For Dedicated customers we default 0% and provide opt-in via console toggle.
jordan: Roll plan: start canary 5% tenants (internal + beta), monitor counters + error rate for a week, then 25%, 50%. Can we expose a quick dashboard?
devin: I'll add a per-tenant telemetry dashboard in console. Will include counters: shim.invoked, shim.fallbacks, shim.latency_p50/p95 (sampled spans).
mike: For cost control, batch exported spans and compress. Also cap events/sec to protect exporters.
sarah: Add a legal note for customers in EU about aggregated telemetry only.
release-bot: deploy started for canary tenant group `compat-telemetry-canary` — build 2026.3.0
ana: ok thanks. Devin, can you create a short RFC about header + sampling semantics? I'll sync with security/privacy before we go wide. :thumbsup:
